newsitem.title: UK: LME zinc meets resistance by close, copper dips.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc meets resistance by close, copper dips.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices marched higher during Monday's trading session but met resistance and profit-taking by the close.
Elsewhere, copper under another LME stocks rise slipped but support at lower levels was evident, while nickel on buy-stops and trade interest after a recent oversold condition forged higher.
"Nothing goes up in a straight line," one LME floor trader said referring to the easing of zinc from seven-year highs of $1,675 a tonne,
By the close of business three months delivery settled at $1,671, well up on Friday's $1,624 close.
Despite the late dip traders said that zinc still has potential to reach $1,700 by the end of this week and possibly $1,800 near-term.

Falling LME stocks, concerns over Chinese short positions and tight nearby dates are likely to keep the market on the boil, though one trader said that he was concerned that the market was ignoring over extended chart signals. "It is strong to the upside but I would like to see some downside correction following the recent massive gains," he said.

Traders said news that China National Nonferrous Metals Corp (CNNC) said it was considering helping Chinese zinc smelters which are holding large short positions was a confirmation of recent talk. They believed they will pay for it eventually or try to trade out of it.
Zinc's cash to three months backwardation during afternoon trading on Monday was fast approching $100, versus $55 on Friday.
Another LME stocks rise impacted on copper which fell prey to general liquidation during LME kerb afternoon trading on Monday.
Final business was at $2,353, below its high of $2,386 and Friday's close of $2,374. Traders said the market was knocked after it failed to move towards $2,400 after Friday's constructive close.
"We had expected the market to move higher but there seemed to be strong overhead selling," a trader said.
Aluminium moved from a high of $1,711 with copper but traders said this was largely a knee jerk reaction. "We had expected resistance above $1,700," one trader commented.
Like copper, alumininm is expected to consolidate at lower levels on Tuesday. Last aluminium business was seen at $1,690, up $5.
Elsewhere, nickel forged ahead as buy-stops against a recent oversold condition kicked in. It was last at $7,395, versus $7,180.
Traders expect nickel to tackle $7,400 and possibly higher on Tuesday.
Lead was quiet during the whole of the session as sister metal held the limelight. It was last at $637, versus $653.
Tin was $10 higher at $5,400, while alloy finished indicated at $1,510/20, versus $1,500/10.
